posts.title: Five new first dans after the autumn grading
posts.excerpt: Three judges, two minutes each and a long wait on the bench.
posts.content:
Seven of our students sat the first dan grading in the town gym on Sunday, and five of them passed. Two were children from the Saturday class, the youngest just thirteen.

What the judges look for is not speed. It is a calm start, a clear shout, a strike with the whole body and the posture after it. The two who did not pass this time will sit again in spring, and the whole class will practise their forms with them.

posts.title: Caring for your armour between practices
posts.excerpt: Air it, never sun it, and tie the cords the same way every time.
posts.content:
Armour that goes straight from practice into a bag starts to smell within a week. Take the helmet and gloves out as soon as you get home and stand them in a shaded, airy place overnight.

Never dry it in the sun: the indigo fades and the leather cracks. Every Sunday morning we open the dojo for mending, with spare cords, leather and a needle for anyone who needs them.

posts.title: Ten mornings of winter practice
posts.excerpt: In the coldest week of the year we practise at six, before school and work.
posts.content:
Winter practice starts on the second Monday of January and runs for ten mornings. The floor is cold enough to sting at first, so we begin by wiping it together; by the third lane nobody notices any more.

Anyone who comes on all ten mornings gets a stamp in the practice book and a bowl of sweet red bean soup on the last day. Children may join with a parent for the first half hour.
